metadata.description: All National Parks managed by the National Park Service.
metadata.author: Journey

journey.name: U.S. National Parks
journey.description: Explore all 63 congressionally designated national parks across the United States and its territories, from iconic mountain and desert landscapes to tropical reefs, ancient forests, caves, and remote Arctic wilderness.

items.name: Acadia National Park
items.description: Granite peaks, rocky Atlantic shoreline, carriage roads, and island forests make Acadia a compact showcase of coastal Maine scenery.

items.name: National Park of American Samoa
items.description: Tropical rainforests, coral reefs, volcanic mountains, and Samoan cultural landscapes stretch across three remote South Pacific islands.

items.name: Arches National Park
items.description: More than two thousand natural stone arches rise above fins, balanced rocks, and high-desert terrain near Moab.

items.name: Badlands National Park
items.description: Layered buttes, sharp pinnacles, mixed-grass prairie, and rich fossil beds create one of the Great Plains' most dramatic landscapes.

items.name: Big Bend National Park
items.description: The Rio Grande bends around desert, canyon, and mountain ecosystems in a vast and remote corner of West Texas.

items.name: Biscayne National Park
items.description: Biscayne Bay protects coral reefs, mangrove shorelines, islands, shipwrecks, and clear subtropical waters best explored by boat.

items.name: Black Canyon of the Gunnison National Park
items.description: The Gunnison River cuts through exceptionally steep, dark Precambrian cliffs, forming a narrow canyon of striking depth and scale.

items.name: Bryce Canyon National Park
items.description: Thousands of colorful hoodoos fill high-elevation amphitheaters beneath some of the clearest night skies in the Southwest.

items.name: Canyonlands National Park
items.description: The Colorado and Green rivers divide a wilderness of mesas, arches, needles, and deeply carved desert canyons.

items.name: Capitol Reef National Park
items.description: A long wrinkle in Earth's crust frames sandstone domes, cliffs, canyons, orchards, and pioneer history in south-central Utah.

items.name: Carlsbad Caverns National Park
items.description: Vast limestone chambers, intricate cave formations, desert wildlife, and seasonal bat flights define this underground New Mexico park.

items.name: Channel Islands National Park
items.description: Five rugged islands preserve sea caves, kelp forests, endemic wildlife, and archaeological resources off Southern California.

items.name: Congaree National Park
items.description: Champion trees, floodplain forest, elevated boardwalks, and quiet waterways protect one of the Southeast's finest old-growth landscapes.

items.name: Crater Lake National Park
items.description: Deep blue water fills the collapsed summit of Mount Mazama, surrounded by cliffs, forests, snowfields, and volcanic features.

items.name: Cuyahoga Valley National Park
items.description: Forests, waterfalls, historic canal paths, farms, and a scenic railroad create an accessible natural corridor between Cleveland and Akron.

items.name: Death Valley National Park
items.description: Salt flats, dunes, colorful badlands, mountain ranges, and North America's lowest point form an immense desert of extremes.

items.name: Denali National Park and Preserve
items.description: North America's highest peak rises above tundra, braided rivers, glaciers, and exceptional habitat for large Alaskan wildlife.

items.name: Dry Tortugas National Park
items.description: Remote islands, coral reefs, turquoise water, seabirds, and massive Fort Jefferson lie nearly seventy miles west of Key West.

items.name: Everglades National Park
items.description: A vast subtropical wetland of sawgrass marshes, mangroves, pinelands, and estuaries supports extraordinary wildlife and water systems.

items.name: Gates of the Arctic National Park and Preserve
items.description: Roadless Arctic wilderness protects sweeping tundra, wild rivers, mountain passes, and traditional homelands above the Arctic Circle.

items.name: Gateway Arch National Park
items.description: The stainless-steel Gateway Arch, historic courthouse, and Mississippi riverfront interpret St. Louis and the nation's westward expansion.

items.name: Glacier National Park
items.description: Glacial valleys, alpine lakes, rugged peaks, wildlife, and the Going-to-the-Sun Road define Montana's northern Rocky Mountains.

items.name: Glacier Bay National Park and Preserve
items.description: Tidewater glaciers, fjords, coastal mountains, marine mammals, and recovering landscapes reveal a dynamic southeast Alaskan wilderness.

items.name: Grand Canyon National Park
items.description: The Colorado River exposes immense layers of geologic history within one of the world's most famous and visually powerful canyons.

items.name: Grand Teton National Park
items.description: The jagged Teton Range rises abruptly above lakes, rivers, sagebrush flats, historic ranches, and abundant wildlife.

items.name: Great Basin National Park
items.description: Ancient bristlecone pines, marble caves, alpine lakes, dark skies, and Wheeler Peak reveal Nevada's remarkable mountain environments.

items.name: Great Sand Dunes National Park and Preserve
items.description: North America's tallest dunes meet seasonal creeks, grasslands, wetlands, forests, and the high peaks of the Sangre de Cristo Range.

items.name: Great Smoky Mountains National Park
items.description: Misty ridges, diverse forests, historic settlements, waterfalls, and renowned biodiversity span the Tennessee-North Carolina border.

items.name: Guadalupe Mountains National Park
items.description: Fossil reef mountains, desert canyons, high-country forest, and Guadalupe Peak preserve a rugged landscape in far West Texas.

items.name: Haleakala National Park
items.description: A vast volcanic summit, high-elevation desert, native species, and lush coastal rainforest stretch from Haleakala's crater to the sea.

items.name: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park
items.description: Active volcanoes, lava fields, rainforests, craters, and Native Hawaiian cultural sites reveal island-building processes in motion.

items.name: Hot Springs National Park
items.description: Historic Bathhouse Row, thermal springs, wooded mountains, and urban trails preserve a long tradition of health and recreation.

items.name: Indiana Dunes National Park
items.description: Lake Michigan beaches, dunes, wetlands, prairies, and forests support exceptional biodiversity along an urbanized shoreline.

items.name: Isle Royale National Park
items.description: A remote Lake Superior archipelago offers wilderness backpacking, paddling, shipwrecks, and a celebrated predator-prey ecosystem.

items.name: Joshua Tree National Park
items.description: The Mojave and Colorado deserts meet among Joshua trees, granite monoliths, cactus gardens, and expansive night skies.

items.name: Katmai National Park and Preserve
items.description: Brown bears gather at salmon streams amid volcanoes, lakes, tundra, and the ash-filled Valley of Ten Thousand Smokes.

items.name: Kenai Fjords National Park
items.description: The Harding Icefield feeds glaciers that descend through coastal mountains into fjords rich with marine wildlife.

items.name: Kings Canyon National Park
items.description: Deep glacial canyons, giant sequoia groves, alpine basins, and Sierra Nevada wilderness surround the Kings River.

items.name: Kobuk Valley National Park
items.description: Great sand dunes rise above the Kobuk River valley along a major caribou migration route in remote Arctic Alaska.

items.name: Lake Clark National Park and Preserve
items.description: Volcanoes, turquoise lakes, glaciers, salmon rivers, coastal bear habitat, and Dena'ina homelands converge southwest of Anchorage.

items.name: Lassen Volcanic National Park
items.description: Lava peaks, hydrothermal areas, mountain lakes, and forests showcase all four major types of volcano in northern California.

items.name: Mammoth Cave National Park
items.description: The world's longest known cave system lies beneath rolling forest, sinkholes, rivers, and a landscape shaped by karst geology.

items.name: Mesa Verde National Park
items.description: Remarkably preserved Ancestral Pueblo cliff dwellings and mesa-top sites document centuries of life in the Four Corners region.

items.name: Mount Rainier National Park
items.description: An ice-clad volcano towers above wildflower meadows, ancient forest, waterfalls, and extensive alpine terrain.

items.name: New River Gorge National Park and Preserve
items.description: A deep Appalachian river gorge combines sandstone cliffs, whitewater, waterfalls, historic communities, and exceptional climbing.

items.name: North Cascades National Park
items.description: Jagged peaks, glaciers, alpine lakes, deep valleys, and dense forests create a rugged wilderness in northern Washington.

items.name: Olympic National Park
items.description: Glaciated mountains, temperate rainforest, wild Pacific coastline, and diverse ecosystems occupy Washington's Olympic Peninsula.

items.name: Petrified Forest National Park
items.description: Colorful badlands, fossilized trees, petroglyphs, and Route 66 history spread across Arizona's high desert.

items.name: Pinnacles National Park
items.description: Volcanic spires, talus caves, chaparral trails, and California condors define a compact mountain landscape inland from the central coast.

items.name: Redwood National and State Parks
items.description: The world's tallest trees stand among fern-filled forests, wild rivers, prairies, and dramatic northern California coastline.

items.name: Rocky Mountain National Park
items.description: High peaks, alpine tundra, glacial lakes, wildlife, and Trail Ridge Road showcase the Colorado Rockies.

items.name: Saguaro National Park
items.description: Giant saguaro forests, desert mountains, cactus blooms, and Sonoran wildlife surround Tucson in two distinct park districts.

items.name: Sequoia National Park
items.description: Giant sequoia groves, deep canyons, marble caves, and the high Sierra include Mount Whitney and the General Sherman Tree.

items.name: Shenandoah National Park
items.description: Skyline Drive follows the Blue Ridge through forests, waterfalls, overlooks, wildlife habitat, and more than five hundred miles of trails.

items.name: Theodore Roosevelt National Park
items.description: Colorful badlands, prairie dog towns, bison, wild horses, and historic ranching landscapes preserve the rugged Little Missouri country.

items.name: Virgin Islands National Park
items.description: Caribbean beaches, coral reefs, tropical forest, historic plantations, and Indigenous sites cover much of St. John.

items.name: Voyageurs National Park
items.description: Interconnected lakes, islands, boreal forest, rocky shorelines, and historic travel routes make this Minnesota park primarily water-based.

items.name: White Sands National Park
items.description: Brilliant gypsum dunes form a constantly shifting white landscape within the Tularosa Basin of southern New Mexico.

items.name: Wind Cave National Park
items.description: A complex cave known for rare boxwork lies beneath mixed-grass prairie supporting bison, elk, and prairie dogs.

items.name: Wrangell-St. Elias National Park and Preserve
items.description: America's largest national park contains immense mountain ranges, glaciers, volcanoes, wild rivers, and historic mining communities.

items.name: Yellowstone National Park
items.description: Geysers, hot springs, wildlife-rich valleys, waterfalls, lakes, and a vast volcanic caldera define the world's first national park.

items.name: Yosemite National Park
items.description: Granite cliffs, waterfalls, giant sequoias, alpine meadows, and deep valleys create one of the Sierra Nevada's most celebrated landscapes.

items.name: Zion National Park
items.description: Towering sandstone walls, narrow canyons, desert terraces, and river-carved trails surround Zion Canyon in southwest Utah.
